entries.75a3f392af923560: KONICA MINOLTA, INC. and 133 [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] and 3 equity-method affiliates make up the group (as of March 31, 2026). Production is handled by production companies in Japan and overseas (such as Konica Minolta Supplies in Yamanashi Prefecture, Konica Minolta Mechatronics in Aichi Prefecture, and manufacturers in China and Malaysia), while sales and services are carried out by regional sales companies, such as Konica Minolta Japan, Konica Minolta Business Solutions U.S.A. in the United States, and Konica Minolta Business Solutions Europe in Europe. Konica Minolta Japan and Konica Minolta Business Solutions U.S.A. are subsidiaries that each account for more than 10% of consolidated revenue. The number of employees in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was 34,363.

entries.76292700e1caaef9: This business develops, manufactures and sells measuring instruments and other equipment, and provides related solutions and services. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 increased from the previous year. The company explains that, as capital investment in displays by major customers recovered, sales of measuring instruments for light source color increased; measuring instruments for object color performed well with new products; and inspection equipment for automotive exterior measurement also expanded sales to new customers. On the other hand, revenue from measuring instruments applying hyperspectral imaging technology declined because customers postponed investment in the European recycling market.

entries.7a41c4a38b1943c6: Revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,087,738 million (¥1.0877 trillion), down 3.6% from ¥1,127,882 million in the previous fiscal year. The company explains that, although revenue in the Industry Business rose, the main factors were the effect of narrowing business areas, including the Professional Print Business, through selection and concentration in the previous fiscal year, and declines in revenue in the Digital Workplace Business and the Imaging Solutions Business. The figures for the previous fiscal year show only continuing operations, with the Precision Medicine Business classified as [[term:discontinued-operations|discontinued operations]].

The company explains that unit sales of digital radiography (DR) were in line with the previous year, and that sales of medical IT grew, mainly in the United States, helped by new products; on the other hand, a decline in demand for X-ray film in China and lower sales of purchased products in Japan had an impact.

entries.b98954f9a79b880c: The company consists of 4 [[term:segment|business segments]]: the Digital Workplace Business, which provides multifunction devices and consumables for offices and IT-related services; the Professional Print Business, which supplies digital printing systems and consumables to the commercial and industrial printing market; the Industry Business, which makes measuring instruments, functional films for displays, industrial inkjet heads, and lenses for industrial and professional use; and the Imaging Solutions Business, which handles medical diagnostic imaging systems, network cameras, video-related equipment, and products and services for nursing care operations. It provides not only equipment but also consumables, services, and solutions.

entries.bd77470ad1d2fd68: Profit attributable to owners of the parent in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥30,268 million (¥30.2 billion), compared with a loss of ¥47,484 million (¥47.4 billion) in the previous fiscal year. The company cites mainly that the recoverability of deferred tax assets for tax losses arising from the selection and concentration of businesses in the previous fiscal year improved, and that tax expenses improved. Also, discontinued operations recorded a loss of ¥1.9 billion (in the previous fiscal year, a profit of ¥45 billion). The consolidated financial statements for this period are prepared under [[term:ifrs|International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)]].
